entries.effect: carried below 9.0 only, where the port's default store exists: from 9.0 the release's own index replaces it and the release has no query over that index, and from 10.0.1 the release has the class itself. A query over the default index: the port's own store, not another application's. Its grammar is the one measured (attribute == and != against a quoted string, * as any run, && binding tighter than ||, parentheses); free text, contains and an unfinished comparison are invalid (CSSearchQueryErrorCodeInvalidQuery). The found handler gets all matches once, when there are some; foundItemCount and the completion error are set before the completion handler runs. A result carries only the fetched attributes. Owed: cancel timing, filterQueries, keyboardLanguage, protectionClasses, items of other applications, the error's user info (see the facts)
entries.source: the macOS CoreSpotlight framework of the host (tests/backports/host/corespotlight-query: 25 lines, identical on both sides after the store root is changed, with a planted control that differs on 2 lines); the rendered CoreSpotlight headers of the 26.2 SDK (spec/CoreSpotlight/declarations.tsv) for the declarations, with -[CSSearchQuery init] declared unavailable there

entries.effect: the codes of CSSearchQueryErrorDomain: -2000 unknown, -2001 index unreachable, -2002 invalid query, -2003 cancelled. The port produces -2002 for a query it does not parse and -2003 for a query cancelled before it answers; -2000 and -2001 it never produces
entries.source: the rendered CoreSpotlight header of the 26.2 SDK (spec/CoreSpotlight/declarations.tsv, the enum and its members) and the host framework's CoreSpotlight.bridgesupport for the values; the port's CSSearchQuery.m compiles against that header with -Werror

entries.effect: a search context with five properties of its own: enableRankedResults, disableSemanticSearch (iOS 18), maxResultCount, maxSuggestionCount, maxRankedResultCount (iOS 18). The factory defaults are measured (maxRankedResultCount 100, maxSuggestionCount 10 with no suggestion); the copy keeps three of the five and the coding keeps disableSemanticSearch only. A non-nil suggestion is owed, because a suggestion comes only from a user query (see the facts)

entries.effect: no class is registered: an application that names CSUserQuery gets an unknown class, and no free-text query is answered (CSSearchQuery's grammar rejects free text)
entries.reason: CSUserQuery: the free-text query whose answers are suggestions, with the engagement callbacks of iOS 18; the port has no class of this name, and the suggestion engine and the free-text answers are not measured
